333400.title: Seymour–Thomas extremal conjecture for complete graph minors
333400.statement:
Let $p\ge1$. A graph is **$(p-2)$-connected** if deleting fewer than $p-2$ vertices leaves it connected. The number of edges in a graph is denoted by $|E(G)|$.

**Seymour–Thomas conjecture.** For every $p\ge1$, there exists a constant $N=N(p)$ such that every $(p-2)$-connected graph on $n\ge N$ vertices and at least

$$
(p-2)n-{p-1\choose2}+1
$$

edges has a $K_p$ minor.

This conjecture seeks a connectivity-sensitive extension of known extremal results for complete graph minors. The source attributes it to Seymour and Thomas and does not state a resolution.
333400.disposition: PARKED: all-p connectivity-sensitive complete-minor theorem; no mechanism paying arbitrary p and large N(p). Low-p or connectivity endpoint repairs cannot resolve full scope.

333401.title: Mader's bound conjecture for complete graph minors
333401.statement:
Let $p\ge1$, and let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **$(p-1)$-colorable** if its vertices can be colored with $p-1$ colors so that adjacent vertices receive different colors.

**Mader's bound conjecture.** For every $p\ge1$, every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least

$$
(p-2)n-{p-1\choose2}+1
$$

edges either has a $K_p$ minor or is $(p-1)$-colorable.

This would extend Mader's extremal bound beyond the cases established in the paper and would imply the authors' corresponding coloring results. The source presents it as a belief and gives no resolution.
333401.disposition: PARKED: arbitrary-p minor-or-colorability dichotomy; no full proof or admissible counterexample. Small p and graph-size convention corrections are not outcomes.

355389.title: The directed Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for tournaments
355389.statement:
Let $H$ be a tournament, meaning an orientation of a complete graph. A tournament is transitive if it contains no directed cycle; an $H$-free tournament contains no induced subtournament isomorphic to $H$.

**Directed Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For every tournament $H$, there exists $epsilon(H)>0$ such that every $H$-free tournament with $n$ vertices contains a transitive subtournament of order at least $n^{epsilon(H)}$.

Alon et al. proved that this tournament formulation is equivalent to the graph formulation of the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The conjecture remains open in general.
355389.disposition: PARKED: all forbidden tournaments H require a polynomial transitive-subtournament exponent; no arbitrary-H induction or obstruction. No protected tournament campaign body read.

329272.title: Erdős–Szemerédi's sunflower conjecture in the Boolean cube
329272.statement:
A **$3$-sunflower** is a collection of three sets having the same pairwise intersections, and $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. **Erdős–Szemerédi's Boolean-cube sunflower conjecture.** There exists an $\varepsilon>0$ such that for every $n\geq 2$, every collection ${\cal F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ with

$$
|{\cal F}|\geq 2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}
$$

contains a $3$-sunflower. This is a special case implied by the classical sunflower conjecture and is itself still open.
329272.disposition: PARKED: need a uniform exponential density saving in the Boolean cube with the exact distinct-set sunflower condition. Fixed-alphabet vector sunflowers in historical neighbors are different predicates; no transfer.

326220.title: Quasigroup formulation of the Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture
326220.statement:
Let $Q$ be a quasigroup of order $n$, with multiplication written multiplicatively, and let $S$ be a subset of triples of the form $(a,b,ab)$ for $a,b\in Q$. A subset of points **spans** a triple in $S$ when all three entries of that triple belong to the subset.

**Quasigroup formulation of the Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture.** For every $c>0$, there is a threshold $n_0$ such that if $Q$ has order $n\geq n_0$, then for every such subset $S$, whenever $|S|\geq cn^2$, some seven-element subset of $Q$ spans at least four triples from $S$.

The source states that this formulation is equivalent to the Brown–Erdős–Sós conjecture. It is the first open case of that conjecture, while the paper proves the assertion for finite groups.
326220.disposition: PARKED: dense arbitrary quasigroup triples need four triples on seven points. Group-case algebra cannot be assumed for quasigroups; no general removal/closure mechanism. Seven-point set/domain corrections excluded.

332511.title: The highly vertically connected matroid minor conjecture
332511.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid. For an integer $k$, $M$ is **vertically $k$-connected** if, for every $A\subseteq E(M)$ with $\lambda_M(A)<k-1$, either $A$ or $E(M)-A$ is spanning in $M$. Write $M(K_n)$ for the cycle matroid of the complete graph, $B(K_n)$ for its bicircular matroid, $U_{n,2n}$ for the uniform matroid, and $M^*$ for the dual matroid. **Highly vertically connected matroid minor conjecture.** For all $n\geq 2$ there is an integer $k$ such that, if $M$ is a vertically $k$-connected matroid with $|M|\geq 2k$, then $M$ or $M^*$ has a minor isomorphic to one of $M(K_n)$, $B(K_n)$, or $U_{n,2n}$. The conjecture predicts the unavoidable minors for highly vertically connected matroids in minor-closed classes omitting a uniform matroid; the dual outcomes reflect that the relevant graph and bicircular matroid duals can have highly vertically connected minors.
332511.disposition: PARKED: highly vertical connectivity does not itself construct one of the three full arbitrary-rank minors in M or dual; no finite witness disproves an unspecified k(n).

382265.title: Polynomial minimal separators or bounded hole length for induced-minor-free graphs
382265.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **clique cutset** is a clique whose deletion disconnects $G$, a **minimal separator** is a minimal vertex set separating two vertices of $G$, and a **hole** is an induced cycle of length at least four. An induced minor of $G$ is obtained by deleting vertices and contracting edges.

**Polynomial-separator or bounded-hole conjecture.** There exists a polynomial $p$ and an integer $k$ such that if $G$ has no clique cutset and does not contain $K_{2,3}$ as an induced minor, then either

$$
|\{S:S\text{ is a minimal separator of }G\}|\leq p(|V(G)|)
$$

or $G$ has no hole of length at least $k$.

This proposes a structural dichotomy for graphs excluding $K_{2,3}$ as an induced minor: graphs without clique cutsets should either have polynomially many minimal separators or have uniformly bounded hole length. The source presents this as an open question; no resolution is given.
382265.disposition: PARKED: a refutation needs arbitrarily long holes simultaneously with superpolynomially many separators, no clique cutset and no induced K2,3 minor. Long cycles alone have polynomial separators; adding many theta-like branches threatens the excluded induced minor. No admissible family proved.

356239.title: The conjecture that PM-VC-Sym is as hard as exact perfect matching
356239.statement:
Let XPM denote exact perfect matching: given a graph with blue/red-colored edges and an integer $k$, determine whether there exists a perfect matching containing exactly $k$ red edges. Let PM-VC-Sym denote perfect matching under vertex-color constraints with symmetric color constraints. Polynomial-time reducibility is denoted by $\le_P$, and polynomial-time equivalence by $=_P$.

**Hardness conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{XPM} =_P \mathrm{PM\text{-}VC\text{-}Sym}.
$$

XPM is known to be in randomized NC, while the paper proves that PM-VC-Sym with a bounded number of colors is also in randomized NC. The conjecture proposes that PM-VC-Sym is no harder than XPM despite allowing more than two colors and bi-colored edges; whether the asserted polynomial-time equivalence holds remains open in the supplied text.
356239.disposition: HOLD: source Theorem10 proves BOUNDED-color equivalence; literal unbounded-color converse unpaid. Base-encoding gadgets and count-vector enumeration are exponential when d varies; NP-hardness is not an unconditional separation.

345465.title: Woodall's circumference conjecture
345465.statement:
Let $G$) be a 2-connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $c(G)$ denote the length of a longest cycle in $G$. **Woodall's conjecture.** If there are at least $\frac{n}{2}+k$ vertices of degree at least $k$, then

$$
c(G)\geq 2k.
$$

This conjecture is proved in the paper as an application of the strengthened Erdős–Gallai theorem.

325281.statement:

$$
n\ge\left\lfloor\frac{8k-2}{3}\right\rfloor,
$$

then every edge-coloring of $K_n$ with four colors contains a 2-colored matching of size $k$. The source presents this as a suspected extremal bound, and its status is not resolved there.

350164.title: Kostochka–Nahvi–West–Zirlin tree reconstructibility conjecture
350164.statement:
Let $\ell$ be a positive integer. A tree is a connected acyclic graph, and it is **$\ell$-reconstructible** if it is determined by its $(n-\ell)$-deck, the multiset of induced subgraphs obtained by deleting $\ell$ vertices.

**Tree reconstructibility conjecture.** For $\ell\ne2$, every tree with at least $2\ell+1$ vertices is $\ell$-reconstructible.

This strengthens Nýdl's conjecture by replacing weak $\ell$-reconstructibility with full $\ell$-reconstructibility. The source presents the assertion as a strengthening and does not state whether it has been resolved.
350164.disposition: PARKED: need injectivity of the (n-ell)-deck map for every tree and every positive ell!=2; recognizable acyclicity does not reconstruct tree isomorphism. No full reconstruction algorithm or equal-deck pair proved.

351824.title: The logarithmic treewidth conjecture for (theta, triangle)-free graphs
351824.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **theta** is a graph consisting of two non-adjacent vertices joined by three paths of length at least two whose interiors are mutually disjoint and pairwise anticomplete. The graph $G$ is **(theta, triangle)-free** if it has neither an induced theta nor an induced triangle. Write $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ for the treewidth of $G$, and let $V(G)$ denote its vertex set.

**Logarithmic treewidth conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that every (theta, triangle)-free graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{tw}(G)\leq c\log(|V(G)|).
$$

The conjecture asks for a logarithmic bound on treewidth in a hereditary graph class. The paper later states that its main theorem settles this conjecture, so its status is solved.

352865.title: Koh–Rogers–Lee–Toh conjecture on graceful variable windmills
352865.statement:
Let $C_n$ be a cycle of length $n\geq 3$, and let $C_n^t$ be the graph obtained from the union of $t$ copies of $C_n$ with one vertex in common, called the central vertex. A graph is **graceful** if it has an injective vertex labelling with labels in $\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$, where $m$ is the number of edges, such that the induced edge labels are exactly $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$. **Koh–Rogers–Lee–Toh conjecture.** The graph $C_n^t$ is graceful if and only if

$$
nt\equiv 0,3\pmod 4.
$$

This conjecture characterizes exactly which variable windmills are expected to admit graceful labellings; the supplied text gives no resolution or partial status, so it remains open.
352865.disposition: PARKED: no all-n,t graceful labeling construction with injectivity and every edge difference exactly once. Parity necessity alone cannot pay sufficiency. Gallian ds6 is unavailable; not fetched or reused.

345466.title: Häggkvist–Jackson strengthening of Woodall's conjecture
345466.statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-connected graph on $n$ vertices. **Häggkvist–Jackson conjecture.** If $G$ contains at least

$$
\max\left\{2k-1,\frac{n+k}{2}+1\right\}
$$

vertices of degree at least $k$, then $G$ has a cycle of length at least

$$
\min\{n,2k\}.
$$

The conjecture strengthens Woodall's circumference condition and is sharp for the two graph constructions described in the paper. Its resolution is not supplied here.
345466.disposition: PARKED: Woodall fan count yields only c>=k+2 in the weak-threshold regime; new attachment/charging lemma needed to reach min(n,2k). Printed source examples miss premise. See sustained derivation.

345467.title: The alpha-generalized Erdős–Gallai path conjecture
345467.statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $x,y\in V(G)$. Let $0<\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}$. **Alpha-generalized path conjecture.** If $G-\{x,y\}$ contains more than $\alpha(n-2)$ vertices of degree at least $k$, then $G$ contains an $(x,y)$-path of length at least

$$
2\alpha k.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of the paper's strengthened Erdős–Gallai theorem, recovering that theorem when $\alpha=\frac{1}{2}$. The paper offers it as a suggested conjecture and gives no resolution.

346086.title: Polynomial-time recognition of supereulerian 2-edge-coloured complete multipartite graphs
346086.statement: A **2-edge-coloured complete multipartite graph** is a complete multipartite graph whose edges are assigned one of two colours, and a graph is **supereulerian** if it contains a spanning eulerian subgraph. **Recognition conjecture.** There exists a polynomial-time algorithm for deciding whether a 2-edge-coloured complete multipartite graph is supereulerian. Despite the existence of a class of examples without an alternating spanning eulerian subgraph, the conjecture proposes polynomial-time recognition for the broader class of 2-edge-coloured complete multipartite graphs.

347048.title: Jackson's degree conjecture for cycles in 2-connected bigraphs
347048.statement:
Let $m,n,b4$ be integers, and let ${\mathcal G}(n,m,b4)$ be the set of bipartite graphs with bipartition $(X,Y)$ such that $|X|=n\geq 2$, $|Y|=m$, and every $x\in X$ has degree at least $b4$. **Jackson's conjecture.** If

$$
b4\geq \max\left\{n,\frac{m+5}{3}\right\},
$$

then every $2$-connected graph $G\in {\mathcal G}(n,m,b4)$ contains a cycle of length $2n$. This conjecture was recently proved, so the stated degree threshold is known to suffice for such a cycle.

343025.title: The standard-example or clique-minor conjecture for posets
343025.statement: Let $P$ be a poset, let $\dim(P)$ denote its dimension, let $S_d$ be the standard example of order $d$, and let the cover graph of $P$ be the graph whose vertices are the elements of $P$ and whose edges are its cover relations. For positive integers $n$ and $d$ with $d\ge2$, **the standard-example or clique-minor conjecture.** There is an integer $d_0$ such that if $\dim(P)\ge d_0$, then either $P$ contains $S_d$ or the cover graph of $P$ contains a $K_n$ minor. This is stated as a considerably stronger conjecture than the planar-poset standard-example conjecture and is presented as open.
343025.disposition: PARKED: arbitrary n,d threshold requires structural control of unbounded poset dimension, not standard-example examples. No uniform bound under both exclusions proved; primary body unread.

344706.title: Projective-geometry embedding conjecture for ideal tangled clutters
344706.statement:
A **tangled clutter** is an ideal clutter with covering number at least two such that every proper deletion minor has covering number one. A clutter $\mathcal{C}$ **embeds $PG(r,2)$** if some subset of its members is a duplication of the cuboid associated with the cocycle space of the projective geometry $PG(r,2)$.

**Projective-geometry embedding conjecture.** There exists an integer $\ell\geq3$ such that every ideal tangled clutter embeds one of $PG(0,2),\ldots,PG(\ell-1,2)$.

The conjecture extends the known $Q_6$ property for a subclass of ideal tangled clutters, namely ideal minimally non-packing clutters with covering number two. It predicts that all ideal tangled clutters contain one of finitely many projective-geometric configurations.
